subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Chinese Water Clocks: Marking Time with Flow
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Chinese Water Clocks: Marking Time with Flow.

hook.text: Before gears, water dripping into bowls measured time for centuries.

buildup.text: Water flowed at a steady rate from one vessel to the next in series.

discovery.text: Su Song's clock tower in 1088 added an escapement driven by water buckets.

twist.text: It combined a water wheel, gear train, and armillary sphere in one tower.

climax.text: It was the most complex machine in the world — 400 years before European clocks.

punchline.text: Water kept time before springs and gears took over.

quiz.question: What made Su Song's clock tower revolutionary?
options: It was the first clock to display seconds
It combined a water-driven escapement with gears and an astronomical display
It used electricity to regulate the flow of water
